name: Protecting Your LA County Solar Investment if the Installer Disappears

mainEntity.name: How do I protect my Los Angeles County solar investment if my installer goes out of business in a few years?
mainEntity.text: How do I protect my Los Angeles County solar investment if my installer goes out of business in a few years?

acceptedAnswer.text: Installer stability is a real concern in the solar industry, including Los Angeles County. To protect yourself if your chosen contractor later closes or rebrands, start by selecting panels, inverters, and batteries from manufacturers with strong balance sheets and clear direct warranty processes. Register your products with the manufacturers immediately after installation so your coverage is on record independently of the installer. Ask for and securely store digital copies of all key documents: signed contract, stamped plans, single-line diagrams, inspection stickers, utility interconnection approvals, and monitoring login credentials. These are essential if a future contractor needs to troubleshoot or if manufacturers request proof for warranty claims. Consider whether your financing provider, equipment manufacturer, or a third-party service company offers ongoing monitoring, maintenance, or warranty administration that is not tied to one installer. Some solar marketplaces or warranty firms can step in to coordinate service if your original contractor disappears. Finally, confirm whether your workmanship warranty is backed solely by the installer or by an insurance-backed program. If it’s only the former and that company fails, workmanship coverage may effectively vanish. By emphasizing strong manufacturers, thorough documentation, and independent support options, you safeguard your system’s long-term performance even through industry shakeups.
